modalities.value: different modalities tokenized for a natural language interface (papers, textbooks, scientific websites, encyclopedias, reference material, knowledge bases, and more)

source.quote: We tokenize different modalities to provide a natural language interface for different tasks.
The models are made available under a non-commercial CC BY-NC 4.0 license.
We train models with sizes ranging from 125M to 120B parameters.

architecture.value: Transformer based architecture in a decoder-only setup with a few modifications

source.quote: Transformer based architecture in a decoder-only setup with a few modifications (see paper for more details).

trainingData.value: 106 billion tokens of open-access scientific text and data (papers, textbooks, scientific websites, encyclopedias, reference material, knowledge bases, and more)

source.quote: The GALACTICA models are trained on 106 billion tokens of open-access scientific text and data.

topics.headline: Often prone to hallucination; high-quality academic corpus does not prevent this

source.quote: As with other language models, GALACTICA is often prone to hallucination - and training on a high-quality academic corpus does not prevent this, especially for less popular and less cited scientific concepts.

topics.headline: No guarantees of truthful output when generating from the model

source.quote: There are no guarantees of truthful output when generating form the model.

topics.headline: Lower toxicity than other large language models (LLMs) but continues to exhibit bias; citation popularity bias at larger scales

source.quote: That being said, the model continues to exhibit bias on certain measures (see the paper for details).

topics.headline: Substantially lower toxicity rates than other LLMs on toxicity benchmarks

source.quote: Overall, the model exhibits substantially lower toxicity rates compared to other large language models.

findings.text: Meta cautions against production use without safeguards because language models can hallucinate.

source.quote: However, we caution against production use without safeguards given the potential of language models to hallucinate.

findings.text: Citation behaviour approaches ground truth with scale, but a popularity bias remains at larger scales.

source.quote: While GALACTICA's citation behaviour approaches the ground truth citation behaviour with scale, the model continues to exhibit a popularity bias at larger scales.

findings.text: On stereotypes and toxicity benchmarks, the model shows substantially lower toxicity rates than other large language models.

source.quote: Overall, the model exhibits substantially lower toxicity rates compared to other large language models.

findings.text: The card claims GALACTICA outperforms several existing language models on knowledge probes, reasoning, and knowledge-intensive scientific tasks, and also on general natural language processing (NLP) versus other open-source general language models (LMs).

source.quote: The model outperforms several existing language models on a range of knowledge probes, reasoning, and knowledge-intensive scientific tasks.

findings.text: Primary intended users are researchers studying language models in the scientific domain; developers building scientific tooling are also anticipated users.

source.quote: The primary intended users of the GALACTICA models are reserachers studying language models applied to the scientific domain.

notes: Source is a short GitHub model card (markdown), not the full galai paper. No numeric eval scores appear in the card; capability and toxicity claims are qualitative and point readers to https://galactica.org/paper.pdf. Parameter table sizes (125M–120B) are model sizes, not evalResults. Seed lists only facebook/galactica-120b; smaller released sizes are that model's checkpoints. Typo in source kept in quotes: 'generating form the model', 'reserachers'.
